# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 64 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47-48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 64

**1** Jesus said: "Someone was hosting a dinner party. Once the meal was ready, he sent his servant to call the guests. The servant went to the first guest and said: 'My master invites you.' The man replied: 'I have dealings with some merchants who are coming to see me tonight. I need to give them my instructions. Please make my apologies.' He went to another and said: 'My master invites you.' That man replied: 'I just bought a house and I have to be there for the day. I won't have time.' He went to another and said: 'My master invites you.' That one said: 'A friend of mine is getting married and I'm organizing the reception. I can't come — please make my apologies.' He went to another and said: 'My master invites you.' He replied: 'I've just bought a farm and I'm going to collect the rent. I can't come — please make my apologies.' The servant came back and reported: 'The people you invited have all sent their regrets.' The master said: 'Then go out into the streets and bring back whoever you come across, so that they can eat.' Buyers and sellers will not enter my Father's domain."

---

**Translator's Notes (PNEUMA):**

- "Dinner party" — social gathering context made vivid
- "Make my apologies" — natural English for asking to be excused
- "My Father's domain" — *topos* rendered as domain/realm rather than "places"
- All four refusals involve commercial or social obligations; the pattern of distraction is clear
